ai.description: Whitaker’s Termite Hill Gecko reaches 50 mm SVL. It is pale brown with dark dorsal crossbands and a white belly. Key features include a slender body, large eyes, and a distinct lack of dorsal tubercles.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus whitakeri* is best distinguished by its lack of enlarged, keeled tubercles on the back, which are present in most other similar Indian *Hemidactylus* species.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus whitakeri* inhabits dry, rocky scrublands and deciduous forests in the Indian peninsula, often found sheltering within termite mounds at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: Whitaker’s Termite Hill Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects while remaining closely associated with termite mounds for shelter.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus whitakeri* is oviparous, laying a single, hard-shelled egg per clutch. Breeding occurs throughout the year, with peak activity during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus whitakeri* is endemic to the northern Western Ghats in Maharashtra, India, typically found at low to moderate elevations.
